name: Break engine
notices: Rule tables derive from measurements of the Groove MIDI Dataset v1.0.0 (Magenta, Creative Commons Attribution 4.0); keep the attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md when copying the module.
third_party: Groove MIDI Dataset (Gillick et al., 2019), CC BY 4.0: derived statistics only, no data files are shipped
threading: Pure functions; thread-safe; not real-time safe (allocates the plan).
platforms: Any C++17 compiler. Bit-identical output across platforms (integer and exact-double arithmetic only).
standalone_test_command: cmake -S modules/break_engine -B build/break_engine && cmake --build build/break_engine && ctest --test-dir build/break_engine
summary: Break-aware rhythm model (engine v2): role-driven 16-step bar plans for drum breaks with backbeat anchors, per-step per-role probability and velocity tables, ghost notes, kick/snare collision rules, 4-bar phrase modifiers, bar-4 fills, fill and glitch gesture tables, six genre profiles, and seeded role-aware swing and microtiming. It plans which role plays where; mapping onto chops and events is done by pattern_engine.
public_api: `planPattern(PlanSettings)` / `planBar(PlanSettings, bar)` -> `BarPlan{hits[]}` with role, step, tick, velocity, gesture tag and anchor flag
`Options` (profile, backbeat variant, anchor mode, groove, humanize, fill, glitch, chaos, phrase strictness, tempo hint) and `valid(Options)`
`canAdd(settings, cells, cell, anchor)`: the collision and density rules, reused by mutate
limits: 16 steps per bar (4/4 on a 16th grid); other meters stay on the legacy engine
Rolls and stutters are separate hits (no retrigger expansion); at most two glitch gestures and one fill per bar
adapters: Map each Hit's role onto a chop of that role (pattern_engine does this) and its velocity onto event level.
adapter_notes: The caller supplies which roles exist (`Avail`) so the plan never asks for a hat the source does not have.
removal: Remove pattern_engine's engine v2 path first (generate_v2.cpp); the legacy engine does not use this module.
